method: Rows 1-15 of ~/codewatch-research/gaps/misses.tsv in file order (the file held 41 work rows, all check-quotes: 30 cve-pairs-python then 11 cve-pairs-python-nonhttp; no JavaScript or PHP rows were reachable in this batch). None was skipped. For each row I read the gap note named in its detail column (benchmarks/gap-notes-2026-11-22-1.json, gap-notes-2026-11-23-1.json, gap-notes-2026-11-23-2.json), the fix commit's message and per-file diff (gh api repos/O/R/commits/SHA, read with 1.5 s between calls) and the source files at the fix commit's parent (gh api repos/O/R/contents/PATH?ref=PARENT, raw), then checked every quoted file:line and code, the category and the probe against them. Six rows needed no correction; nine had at least one field corrected: three categories (source/check to functions, because the note's own probe is found by codewatch so the miss is the cross-file flow), two source lines, three sink lines, two between steps, two fix descriptions and one probe (a Flask JSON source where the case reads a protobuf body).

notes.category: wrong: functions - the note's own probe (a FastAPI body field exec'd in the same file) is found by codewatch, so the Pydantic body field is a known source and exec a known sink; in the real flow the body field code.code is read in langflow/api/v1/validate.py and exec()'d in the separate lfx package (lfx/custom/validate.py), so the value crosses files and packages

notes.probe:
wrong: import os
from flask import Flask, request
from mlflow.protos.service_pb2 import StartTraceV3

app = Flask(__name__)
ROOT = "/tmp/mlruns"

@app.post("/mlflow/traces")
def start_trace():
    msg = StartTraceV3.FromString(request.get_data())
    trace_id = msg.trace.trace_info.trace_id
    d = os.path.join(ROOT, "traces", trace_id)
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    return {"ok": True}

notes.category: wrong: functions - the note's own probe (request.get_json() into open() in one file) is found by codewatch, so strip/replace is not taken for sanitizing; in the real flow the admin API value goes through db.edit, make_editor_session, EditorSession.get_fs_path and pad.db.to_fs_path before untrusted_to_os_path in another file, and the write is atomic_open in editor.py again
notes.fix: wrong: make_editor_session rejects a path that parse_path would not reproduce (raises BadEdit) and untrusted_to_os_path rebuilds the path from cleanup_path instead of strip/replace; the diff adds no containment check against the content root (the new assert clean_path.startswith('/') always holds after cleanup_path)

notes.sink: wrong: resolverapi/endpoints.py:53-55 abort(400, message="%s type is not supported" % rdtype) and abort(400, message="%s is not a valid domain name" % domain), the second abort at line 55 (the note's 54 is the is_valid_hostname test); resolverapi/endpoints.py:96 abort(400, message="%s is not a valid ip address" % ip) in ReverseLookup.valid_args (94-96) - the request value is interpolated into the error message

notes.source: wrong: backend/open_webui/routers/terminals.py:253-258 @router.websocket('/{server_id}/api/terminals/{session_id}') async def ws_terminal(ws: WebSocket, server_id: str, session_id: str) - the WebSocket route path parameter session_id comes from the client; policy_id does not, it is read from the saved connection config at terminals.py:281 (connection.get('policy_id')) and the note's 285-294 are the body of the function

notes.between: wrong: utils.from_params -> QueryParser().parse(params['q']) in postgres/queryparser.py:182-184 at the fix's parent, where parse() returns repr(query_expr.parseString(query)[0]).replace('__default_field__', default_field) (the note's 283-288 are lines of the post-fix file); repr() of the parsed tree leaves the raw search terms concatenated into the WHERE string -> Query(where=..., vars={}) -> base.py SELECT ... WHERE {query.where} -> _fetchall -> cursor.execute. The value crosses utils.py, queryparser.py and base.py and is never passed as a parameter

notes.category: wrong: functions - codewatch finds the note's probe (a FastAPI path parameter into run(..., shell=True) in one file), so the double quotes are not taken for sanitizing; in the real flow the path is read by the /git/diff route, formatted into the command by GitHandler.get_git_diff in git_handler.py and executed by run() in git_diff.py, crossing files
notes.source: wrong: openhands/server/routes/files.py:301-308 @app.get('/git/diff') async def git_diff(path: str, ...) - the path query parameter is read by that route and passed at line 322 to runtime.get_git_diff(path, cwd); the note's 267-277 are the sibling git_changes endpoint
notes.between: wrong: API route -> GitHandler.get_git_diff (git_handler.py:141 result = self.execute(self.git_diff_cmd.format(file_path=file_path), self.cwd), not 137-140) -> git_diff.py -> run(); the double quotes around the path in run(f'git show "..."') look like shell quoting but a path containing a double quote closes them and the rest is interpreted by the shell
notes.fix: wrong: shlex.quote()s the ref:path argument in git_diff.py (_make_git_show_cmd) and the file_path in git_handler.py before the command string is built; the command is still run as a shell string, not as an argument list
